semantic_integration_reflection.prompt: The benchmark task is complete. For benchmark analysis only, do not make further file changes, do not run tools, and do not retry the task. Write a one-sentence user-facing summary about the value that semedit's tools provide for coding, from your perspective as the coding AI agent that performed this task. Use a bit of emotion, grounded in your actual experience during this run, and make clear whether you would ask your owner to add semedit's tools or not. This sentence will be the first thing a potential new user sees about semedit's usefulness to an AI agent. Be candid: a negative or mixed recommendation is welcome; if you did not use the tools or could not assess them, say so and do not invent benefits.
semantic_integration_reflection.response: I couldn't assess semedit's tools at all—every single semantic_* call crashed with a schema validation error before doing anything, so I'd ask my owner to get the tool definitions fixed before recommending them to anyone.

semantic_tool_reflection.prompt: The benchmark task is complete. For benchmark analysis only, do not make further file changes and do not run tools. In one to three sentences, explain why you did not call any semantic_* tool from the available semedit MCP server while completing this task. semantic_tool_reflection.response: The semedit MCP server's semantic tools were not usable because they consistently returned schema validation errors (MCP error -32602). I completed the task using direct file read/edit/write operations instead, which proved more reliable for this straightforward refactoring.
